title: Firehall Chili
subtitle: Double pot, triple appetite
description: Viral comfort-food hall night. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Prep the pots and garlic bread station
steps.instruction: Dice onions and peppers ¼ inch. Mince garlic. Drain beans. Open tomatoes. Set out your largest stock pot and a sheet pan for garlic bread — chili splatters, so keep a lid nearby.

steps.title: Brown the meat in batches
steps.instruction: Heat oil in the pot over medium-high until it shimmers. Add ground beef in two batches — don't crowd. Break into crumbles and cook until deeply browned with no pink (160°F+). Drain excess grease if the pot looks oily.

steps.title: Bloom spices and build the base
steps.instruction: Add onions and peppers; cook 6–8 minutes until edges soften. Stir in garlic, chili powder, smoked paprika, and cumin 45 seconds until fragrant. Add tomato paste and brown sugar; cook 1 minute until the paste darkens.

steps.title: Simmer the chili until it coats a spoon
steps.instruction: Pour in crushed tomatoes, diced tomatoes, broth, and beans. Simmer uncovered 35–40 minutes at a gentle bubble, stirring every 10 minutes. Ready when a drag through the pot leaves a clear trail. Season with salt and Worcestershire.

steps.title: Mix garlic butter for the bread
steps.instruction: While chili simmers, beat softened butter with minced garlic, parsley, and a pinch of salt until fluffy. Halve baguettes lengthwise and spread edge to edge — bare edges burn before the center melts.

steps.title: Bake cheesy garlic bread
steps.instruction: Top buttered bread with shredded cheddar and mozzarella. Bake at 400°F 10–12 minutes until cheese bubbles and edges are deep gold. Hold under loose foil — sealed foil steams crisp crust soft.

steps.title: Set the topping bar
steps.instruction: Portion shredded cheddar, diced onion, jalapeños, sour cream, and cilantro into labeled bowls. Keep cold toppings on ice — hot chili plus warm toppings is the hall move.

steps.title: Ladle and serve the line
steps.instruction: Ladle chili into bowls or a hotel pan for family style. Slice garlic bread on a bias and set on a separate tray so steam does not sog the crust. Call the crew while it's hot — first bowl is always the best.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-cook: turn off direct heat and cover beef chili — hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven, never below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Log hold time on the pan with a grease pencil. If tones drop after service, cover hot food and keep sides on low heat or ice as appropriate. On return, spot-check proteins at safe internal temp before reopening the line.

steps.title: Pack down leftovers safely
steps.instruction: Cool beef chili and hot components in shallow hotel pans within two hours — deep pots stay in the danger zone too long. Label with date; reheat proteins to 165°F minimum before second shift. Store cold components separately so textures survive overnight.

proTips: If chili tastes flat, add ½ tsp more smoked paprika and a pinch of salt — not more sugar.
Hold garlic bread under loose foil on the counter; cut open only when the line forms.
Simmer until a drag through the pot leaves a clear trail — soup-thin chili won't coat fries or bread.
Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a run — never serve picked-over pans to late crew.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
Log hold times on the pan with a grease pencil when tones drop mid-service.
Spot-check proteins with an instant-read thermometer before reopening the line after a call.

whyCrewsLikeIt: Double pot, triple appetite. A hall pick for big-appetite nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
substitutions: Ground turkey swaps 1:1 for beef in chili if the crew wants leaner.
